title: How to write an intensity or cumulative intensity function for vectorized models
text: population person carries frailty shape parameter, model sampled thinning (lambda known) inversion (closed-form Lambda inverse): λi(t)=witpi\lambda_i(t) = w_i \, t^{p_i}, Λi(t)=witpi+1/(pi+1)\Lambda_i(t) = w_i \, t^{p_i + 1} / (p_i + 1).

title: Simulating Nonhomogeneous Poisson Point Processes
text: nhppp package simulating events one dimensional nonhomogeneous Poisson point processes (NHPPPs). functions based three algorithms provably sample target NHPPP: time-transformation homogeneous Poisson process (intensity one) via inverse integrated intensity function; generation Poisson number order statistics fixed density function; thinning majorizing NHPPP via acceptance-rejection scheme. developed provide fast memory efficient functions discrete event statistical simulations. description algorithms numerical comparison R packages, see Trikalinos Sereda (2024), accessible https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.00358.

text: Simulates events one dimensional nonhomogeneous Poisson point processes (NHPPPs) per Trikalinos Sereda (2024, doi:10.48550/arXiv.2402.00358  2024, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0311311 ). Functions based three algorithms provably sample target NHPPP: time-transformation homogeneous Poisson process (intensity one) via inverse integrated intensity function (Cinlar E, "Theory stochastic processes" (1975, ISBN:0486497996)); generation Poisson number order statistics fixed density function; thinning majorizing NHPPP via acceptance-rejection scheme (Lewis PAW, Shedler, GS (1979) doi:10.1002/nav.3800260304 ).

text: CRAN release: 2026-11-15 Unify sc-step C++ kernels; separate reporting count conditioning (report_first_K/report_last_K vs generate_at_least_K/generate_at_most_K); rename atmostB budget_cap New features — two orthogonal truncation option classes - REPORTING (report_first_K, report_last_K; one may set): return earliest / latest min(N, K) events realization. reporting truncations — count law sampled process unchanged. atmost1 remains alias report_first_K = 1. - GENERATION conditioning (generate_at_least_K, generate_at_most_K; combinable K1 <= K2): change sampled law X | K1 <= N <= K2. generate_at_least_K = 1 alone zero-truncated case (atleast1 remains alias); generate_at_least_K = generate_at_most_K = K conditions exactly K events — object reporting first K N >= K draw (reported-first-K times biased early relative exactly-K law). Conditioned sampling uses exact order-statistics construction doubly-truncated Poisson count, drawn inversion CDF restricted truncation region (upper-tail parameterization, numerically stable deep right tail; primitives rbtpois() R rbtpois/rbtpois_vec C++). generation bound routes order-statistics kernels; without generation bounds sequential inversion kernels used (condition future total). - vdraw_cumulative_intensity() supports full option set: generation bound switches sequential inversion exact order-statistics construction Lambda scale (doubly-truncated Poisson count; ascending uniforms (Lambda(t_min), Lambda(t_max)) drawn normalized Exp(1) spacings mapped Lambda_inv), report_last_K honored paths. - vectorized thinning samplers support generation bounds rejection resampling (proposals push lower bound majorizer; accepted-count condition verified per row). scalar thinning samplers support generate_at_least_K = 1. - scalar samplers ppp(), draw_sc_linear(), draw_sc_loglinear(), draw_cumulative_intensity() draw_intensity() accept full option set (report_first_K, report_last_K, atleast1, generate_at_least_K, generate_at_most_K), like draw_sc_step() draw(). generation bound routes zero-truncated twin (ztppp(), ztdraw_sc_linear(), ztdraw_sc_loglinear(), ztdraw_cumulative_intensity()); draw_intensity() supports generate_at_least_K = 1. new arguments follow existing ones, calls use return draws . - budget_cap replaces atmostB (soft-deprecated alias warning): caps computational event budget vectorized kernels approximation knob (jointly 1 - tol quantile bound), exact reporting conditioning contract. now honored uniformly vectorized sc-step paths (whole-range regular path used ignore atmostB silently) never truncates conditioned count generate_at_least_K. Internals - eight sc-step C++ kernels (regular/general x plain/zt x whole-range/subinterval) unified two template algorithm cores two grid policies (src/sc_step_core.h); whole-range sampling subinterval special case. Net deletion ~300 lines performance loss: whole-range paths ~6x faster (fixed-size blocked Exp(1) draw replaced lazy per-event draws), zero-truncated paths ~1.5x faster, subinterval paths ~1.2x faster included benchmark (benchmarks/bench_sc_step_unify.R). - zero-truncated kernels now honor tol instead hard-coded .99999 event-count quantile. - Test infrastructure: sample-validity helper checks matrices whole-matrix operations instead per-row testthat expectations (suite drops ~15 minutes ~15 seconds 10^4-row distributional fixtures), distributional tests (Q-Q agreement, chi-square, Kolmogorov-Smirnov assertions) skipped CRAN. - Copy/allocation fixes: per-event row materialization interval search, fused Lambda construction, dead matrix pre-allocations, column trimming skips copy nothing trimmed, 1-row range_t/t_min/t_max inputs shared across rows instead replicated R level. - New -demand R-hub v2 workflow (.github/workflows/rhub.yaml) sanitizer valgrind checks. unified kernels clean clang-ASan, gcc-ASan, valgrind (one valgrind finding small leak rstream dependency, nhppp code). Structured argument containers user functions - args containers (lambda_args, Lambda_args) now two explicit channels: shared (named list row-invariant arguments type, stored never replicated across point processes) row_args (data.frame data.table one row per point process, validated row count automatically row-subset rejection loops). container passed user function’s SECOND POSITIONAL argument, exactly given except row_args already subset; name second formal user’s choice. - Deprecations compatibility: flat list neither recognized element keeps released -shared behavior warning (thinning family); nested vector_arguments data.table convention deprecated (mapped onto row_args semantics, warning per call); Lambda_inv_args deprecated — one Lambda_args container delivered Lambda Lambda_inv. vdraw_cumulative_intensity(), flat/legacy containers keep released named-argument call (Lambda(t, Lambda_args = ...)) deprecation warning; structured containers get positional call. arguments supplied , user functions now called single argument (Lambda(t) instead Lambda(t, Lambda_args = NULL)), plain one-argument closures work everywhere. - row_args/vector_arguments accept plain data.frames (data.table requirement dropped; data.tables still accepted -, read-, never coerced copied). - New vignette “write intensity cumulative intensity function vectorized models”: calling contract, structured container alignment idiom, majorizer construction, worked thinning-vs-inversion example, anti-patterns. - get_step_majorizer() gains fun_args, taking container delivery convention, sampler’s lambda can used majorizer construction without hand-wrapping. Thinning (intensity) family - New vdraw_intensity_step(): vectorized thinning sampler piecewise constant majorizers arbitrary interval bounds (time_breaks, vdraw_sc_step()); target intensity remains arbitrary vectorized R function. Generalizes vdraw_intensity(), assumes equal-length intervals. share one C++ template core (src/intensity_step_core.h). - Count conditioning vectorized thinning samplers (vdraw_intensity(), vdraw_intensity_step()): conditioning rejection — candidate realizations proposed majorizer conditioned least K1 majorizer events (exact: lower bound may pushed proposal), thinned, rows whose accepted count falls outside [K1, K2] resampled. per-round acceptance probability degrades strictness bounds looseness majorizer; iteration cap. Special case K1 = K2 = K (exactly K events): -counts rejected — rows K survivors salvaged exactly keeping uniformly random size-K subset events (conditionally-iid times make subset exact exactly-K draw regardless surviving count, knowledge integrated target intensity), avoiding near-zero two-sided acceptance probability target integrated intensity large relative K. scalar thinning samplers support generate_at_least_K = 1. - thinning kernels now error lambda exceeds majorizer also conditioned path (old R-zero-truncated path silently capped acceptance probabilities 1, sampling wrong process majorizer invalid). internal vdraw_intensity_step_regular_forcezt() removed, superseded conditioned C++ kernel. Long-format output vectorized samplers - New output = c("matrix", "long") argument sc-step samplers (vdraw_sc_step(), vztdraw_sc_step(), vdraw_sc_step_regular() _cpp kernels) vdraw_cumulative_intensity() / vdraw(). "long" returns list(id, time, n_draws) one entry per event: id 1-based point-process index (ascending, times ascending within id). point process zero events contributes entries — id absent, n_draws distinguishes “events” “sampled”; NA used. C++ paths build long format directly (dense intermediate; accumulator reserve()d expected Lambda mass), preferred event counts vary widely across point processes: included benchmark (10^6 processes, mean ~1 event, max ~40), 404 MB dense vs 11.5 MB long, ~30% faster. RNG consumption identical across two outputs, -seed dense long draw hold event values. conditioned vdraw_cumulative_intensity() path, Lambda_inv called event vector row_args subset one row per event (aligned id). thinning samplers take output yet. - New vignette “Long event output large simulations” showing two formats side side, -event semantics, memory/time comparison event-count heterogeneity grows. Documentation - Reference examples modernized current API: draw(), vdraw(), vdraw_cumulative_intensity() gain examples (none); structured args containers, generation bounds (including exactly-K), reporting truncations, get_step_majorizer(fun_args = ) now demonstrated reference pages. Vignette code uses budget_cap reporting/generation vocabulary throughout. Breaking change (random streams ) - -seed results differ 1.0.5.x vectorized sc-step, zero-truncated, thinning samplers: package guarantees sampled process distribution, number order RNG calls. Users relying common random numbers block RNG streams . Generalize vectorized sc-step samplers arbitrary interval bounds; fix four latent bugs New features - Add vdraw_sc_step() vztdraw_sc_step(): vectorized sampling piecewise constant intensities intervals need equally spaced. time_breaks argument accepts vector K+1 bounds shared point processes, n x (K+1) matrix one row bounds per point process (1-row matrix treated shared replicated memory; C++ kernels index row 0 directly). - lambda_matrix (per-interval rates) Lambda_matrix (cumulative interval ends) forms supported, t_min/t_max subintervals, atmost1, atmostB, atleast1 (routes zero-truncated sampler), matching vdraw_sc_step_regular() interface. - New vignette “Step intensities arbitrary intervals” showcasing vdraw_sc_step() / vztdraw_sc_step() standard demographic age bands, timing study vdraw_sc_step_regular(). - Implementation: new C++ kernels (vdraw_sc_step_general[2], vztdraw_sc_step_general[2], step_general_inverse, find_break_interval) mirror *_regular kernels three regularity operations replaced: per-interval widths rate--cumulative conversion, binary search breaks time--interval lookup, breaks-based index+fraction--time reconstruction. Existing *_regular kernels untouched, previously drawn seeds reproduce exactly. Bug fixes (regression test) - vdraw_intensity_step_regular_cpp() / vdraw_intensity() / vdraw(): thinning step looked majorizer wrong interval whenever interval length differed 1 (misplaced parenthesis index arithmetic), distorting acceptance ratio throwing “Majorizer error”. Draws functions change (now correct) interval length 1. - vdraw_sc_step_regular_cpp() / vztdraw_sc_step_regular_cpp(): subinterval bound equal rate_matrix_t_max read past end cumulative-intensity row (--bounds read). Indices fractions now clamped; results previously-correct inputs unchanged. - vdraw(): supplying Lambda_maj_matrix now routes thinning sampler documented instead erroring (dispatch condition tested lambda_maj_matrix twice). - vztdraw_intensity() (internal): range_t passed vztdraw_intensity_step_regular() every call errored. Tests validation - New test files cover shared per-row breaks, subintervals, argument validation, seed reproducibility, rlecuyer streams, cross-validation: -seed agreement *_regular kernels equal-spaced breaks, bitwise shared-vs-replicated-breaks equality, distributional agreement scalar draw_sc_step(). - Full suite: 36,367 assertions, 0 failures; R CMD check: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.
